# storage-core: ArrayStorage contract, Index, OutBuf, StridedBuf, Plain / Scalar / Any / forwarders

Paths are under jix/src unless they start with jix-py/. "NEW" = new or rewritten since 6dbeb15.

## Purpose

`ArrayStorage` (core_trait.rs:54) is the sealed trait every backend and lazy op implements:
`shape()`, `dtype()`, `read_data(index, ctx, out)` plus hidden `read_as_elementwise_pipeline`,
`spec`, `info`, `as_compact`, `element_type_change`. NEW: the region is an `Index` (index.rs:16,
start + non-zero size per dim) and the destination an `OutBuf` (buf.rs:450, push `&mut StridedBuf`
or pull `&mut Option<StridedBuf>` slot); `read_data` returns `Result<()>`. `StridedBuf` (buf.rs:46)
= bytes + per-dim usize byte strides, no shape. Leaf backends: `Plain` (plain.rs:55, zero-copy view
of caller memory), `Scalar` (scalar.rs:30, one value broadcast). Forwarders: NEW `&S` / `&mut S`
(replace the removed `View`), `Box`/`Rc`/`Arc` (mod.rs:99-174), `&dyn ArrayStorage`
(mod.rs:176-215), `ArrayStorageAny` (any.rs:17). `ArrayStorageExt` (core_trait.rs:165-200, NEW)
gives `read_data_pull` / `read_data_pull_in` / `read_data_push`.

## Contracts

Index (index.rs, NEW):
- Invariant (doc index.rs:13-14): `start.len() == size.len() <= NDIM_MAX`, every size >= 1,
  `start + size` fits u64. It says NOTHING about a shape: in-bounds is checked by each storage.
- `Index::new` (pub, :31) checks all of it (`check`, :52-63). `new_unchecked` (pub(crate) unsafe,
  :44) only `debug_assert`s; it transmutes `&[usize]` to `&[NonZeroUsize]` (:47). `start()` /
  `size()` run `assert_unchecked(len equal && <= NDIM_MAX)` (:91-95): a mismatched-length index
  built through `new_unchecked` is UB in release, not a panic. `end()` (:86) adds unchecked.
- Who guarantees non-empty: the Array front doors, after `check_ranges` (error.rs:228-246: ndim
  <= 8, start <= end <= shape, length fits usize): `to_ndarray_sub` (array/read.rs:182, 231, 255-256),
  `to_buf_slice` (:314-321), `to_buf_strided` (:383-389, empty -> `alloc_empty`),
  `to_buf_strided_into` (:447-454, empty -> only `check_out_buf_dims`). `split_ranges`
  (index.rs:99-103) does unchecked `end - start` and a truncating `as usize`: only valid after
  `check_ranges` (all non-test callers are those four). Compaction builds chunk indices from an
  NdIter that yields nothing when a dim is 0 (array/compact.rs:248-265); the slow path builds
  pieces at array/read.rs:522-554. Every op derives sub-indices with `new_unchecked` and must keep
  sizes >= 1 and lengths equal: permute_dims.rs:133, insert_dim.rs:175, remove_dim.rs:173,
  slice.rs:142/162/209, broadcast.rs:145, tile.rs:150/183/198, concatenate.rs:241/321,
  roll.rs:109/140, stack.rs:219, flip.rs:116, reshape.rs:367, repeat.rs:136,
  reduction/common.rs:562 (all under ops/).
- `read_data` is pub but uncallable outside the crate: `OutBuf` has only pub(crate) constructors
  (buf.rs:450-467). Users read through array/read.rs; jix-py too (jix-py/src/array.rs:646).

read_data contract (doc core_trait.rs:70-92) - every impl MUST:
1. Call `check_out_buf(&out, self.shape(), index, itemsize)` (buf.rs:352-364) before touching
   memory: `check_get_range` (error.rs:249: ndim match, `end <= shape`), `check_region_size`
   (error.rs:298: 32-bit only, prod(size) * itemsize <= isize::MAX; no-op on 64-bit), and for push
   `check_out_buf_impl` (buf.rs:384-431): stride count == ndim and writable
   (`check_out_buf_dims`, :367-381), strides non-overlapping over the region (`disjoint_span`,
   :398-403, dims of len 1 ignored, conservative), and that span <= `out.data().0.len()`.
   Exception: Compact enters `read_cached` first (compact.rs:246) and checks in
   `read_data_uncached` (compact.rs:309); the cache-hit path runs only `check_out_buf_impl`
   (context.rs:189) and relies on a hit implying a previously validated index.
2. Pull: on Ok, fill the slot exactly once. `write_out_buf_slot` (buf.rs:505-515) asserts the slot
   was empty (after `mem::forget` of the old value); `read_data_pull(_in)` panics if it is still
   empty (core_trait.rs:174, 192-194). The buffer must hold initialized bytes for `index.size()`
   at its strides; it may borrow `self`/`context` for `'a`; if writable, its strides must not
   alias over the region (else `make_readonly`, buf.rs:176).
3. Push: write every byte of every element of the region (padding included) at out's own strides
   from out's byte 0, write nothing else, and do not replace `*out` or change its strides (the
   caller keeps using its own buffer: `to_ndarray_sub` `assume_init`s the uninit ndarray,
   array/read.rs:231-243; compaction compresses an uninit chunk buffer, array/compact.rs:258-273).
4. On Err the slot may hold a partial buffer and out may be partly written; callers discard.

OutBuf (buf.rs:449-501, NEW): `Push(&'s mut StridedBuf<'a>)` is invariant in `'a`, so a push read
runs at the out buffer's lifetime. `materialize` (:475-488, safe): push returns the caller's out
unchanged (assumes rule 1 ran); pull allocates via `alloc_out_buf` (:434-447): uninitialized
pool buffer of `prod(shape) * itemsize` bytes (unchecked usize multiply) at
`strides_for_layout_order` (util/mod.rs:164-179; non-aliasing only if `layout_order` is a
permutation - only its length is debug_asserted). `set` (:491-500, safe): pull puts `data` in the
slot; push does an unsafe `copy_from` that relies on the caller having checked out and `data`
holding the region (single caller context.rs:192).

StridedBuf unsafe fns (who must establish the precondition):
- `from_raw_parts` (pub, buf.rs:78) / `from_raw_parts_mut` (pub, :101): `data` non-null, valid
  for the strided span of (shape, strides, itemsize) for `'a`, not mutated during `'a`; `_mut`:
  exclusive, no overlap with any array of the lazy chain, strides do not alias. Caller: users,
  jix-py numpy(out=). The slice length is `strided_span_bytes` (util/mod.rs:105-123: 0 for an
  empty shape, zips shape with strides, unchecked `stride * (len-1)`); more than 8 strides panics
  in `to_dim_vec`.
- `from_slice` (:119) / `from_shared` (:161): every access implied by strides and the read shape
  in bounds. `from_slice_mut` (:135) / `from_pool` (:148): plus no aliasing. Callers: this
  subsystem, context.rs:185/232, array/read.rs, array/compact.rs, most ops.
- `set_strides` (:257, NEW, replaces `with_strides`): new strides keep the from_slice_mut contract
  for a writable buffer; call `make_readonly` first for aliasing strides. Callers: buf.rs:544,
  broadcast.rs:161 (after make_readonly), slice.rs:170 (no make_readonly).
- `copy_from` (:269): both stride sets in bounds for `shape`, lengths == shape.len(). Its Safety
  text omits `NdCopier::copy`'s no-overlap rule (nd_copy.rs:51-52) and dtype class match.
- `with_offset` (:296): result valid for the same shape/strides; Slice variants panic if n > len,
  PoolBuf/Shared variants defer the panic to `data()`.
- `read_data_and_map_strides` (:532-554, NEW body): the closures produce strides valid for the
  inner region (push) / output region (pull, buffer may be writable). Callers:
  permute_dims.rs:131, insert_dim.rs:173, remove_dim.rs:171.

Other unsafe fns: `Plain::new` (pub, plain.rs:109), `Array::plain_ndarray_ptr` (pub,
plain.rs:413): pointer valid for the Plain's life, every element of `0..shape[d]` readable and a
valid `dtype` value (ptr variant), the whole strided span in ONE allocation, not written or
`&mut`-borrowed while read or while a pull view is alive (plain.rs:97-108, 417-427). Alignment
NOT required. `plain_ndarray_ref_impl` (private, :278): `'a` matches the borrowed data.

Relied on from elsewhere: `tune` (params.rs:282-291) checks ndim, non-zero itemsize and
`check_shape_overflow` (error.rs:192: product*itemsize fits u64, every dim <= i64::MAX) for every
Plain/Scalar shape; `into_spec` hard-asserts block-shape sanity (params.rs:499-510);
`ElementType` is sealed (element_type.rs:16) so `Ty<T>::dtype() == T::DTYPE`; `unsafe trait
Dtyped` promises size/alignment; `OperandTyped::new_input` needs valid T bytes for the region
(ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs:812-818).

## Unsafe inventory

- core_trait.rs:124 `OperandTyped::new_input` - dtype checked at :129; byte validity = pull
  contract of every impl (non-local; ArrayStorage sealed so only crate impls).
- index.rs:34 `new_unchecked` after `check` - local. :47, :77 slice transmutes usize <->
  NonZeroUsize - layout identical; :47 validity rests on callers (non-local, debug_assert only).
  :92-94 `assert_unchecked` - rests on every `new_unchecked` caller (non-local).
- buf.rs:85, 108 raw slice from computed span - user contract. :86, :109 from_slice(_mut).
- buf.rs:119-165, 257, 296 constructors / relabels - callers only, no runtime check.
- buf.rs:277-286 `NdCopier::copy` via `copy_from` - bounds and non-overlap from callers: Plain push
  (plain.rs:469, Plain contract + check_out_buf), Scalar strided push (scalar.rs:117, 0 strides),
  `OutBuf::set` (buf.rs:497, cache buffer vs checked out), Broadcast push (broadcast.rs:167).
- buf.rs:446 `from_pool` - pool capacity >= requested size (buf_pool.rs:39-50); size is an
  unchecked usize product, bounded by check_region_size only on 32-bit.
- buf.rs:497 `copy_from` inside SAFE `OutBuf::set` - non-local (context.rs:189-192).
- buf.rs:544 `set_strides`, :550 `from_slice_mut` over `out.data_mut()` - caller closures.
- PoolBuf/PoolBufShared `as_slice` (buf_pool.rs:108-118, 147-151) expose the whole pool capacity,
  uninitialized bytes included, as `&[u8]`; `StridedBuf::data()` (buf.rs:207-216) hands that out.
- any.rs:61 `assert_unchecked(len <= NDIM_MAX)` - `DimDyn::from_slice` panics past 8 at
  construction (any.rs:105).
- scalar.rs:99, 120 `cast_slice::<T,u8>` of `self.data` - exposes T's padding bytes (uninit for
  padded `#[repr(C)]` structs). :115 `cast_slice_mut::<u8,T>` - alignment and length asserted
  (util/mod.rs:209-219, panic not UB); length bounded by `[..region_len]`.
- scalar.rs:136 `transmute_copy::<T,T2>` - `check_dtype` at :138 plus the Dtyped layout promise.
- plain.rs:178 `SendSyncPtr::new` - Plain is Send+Sync whenever A and ET are (util/mod.rs:525-532).
- plain.rs:240 `ptr.add(offset)` from `into_raw_vec_and_offset` - ndarray guarantees.
- plain.rs:460 `ptr.add(offset)` + `from_raw_parts(.., span)` - Plain contract + check_get_range +
  size >= 1 (Index invariant; only `debug_assert!(size != 0)` at :471). Slice covers gap bytes:
  K111 (open).
- plain.rs:281, 347, 388, 439 constructor chains - lifetime tied to `&'a ArrayBase` / ArrayView.

## Edge-case surface

- Empty regions: never reach a storage (Index). Plain lost its span-0 special case (NEW,
  plain.rs:448-460 assumes size >= 1); empty Plain arrays are still constructible (any stride,
  plain.rs:513-517) but every Index into them fails `check_get_range`.
- 0-d (shape []): `Index::new(&[], &[])` is valid (test compact.rs:1040); Plain span = itemsize,
  offset 0; Scalar `region_len` = size_of::<T>() (empty product); `disjoint_span` over no dims =
  itemsize; `alloc_out_buf` allocates 1 element; `is_contiguous` compares empty strides.
- Length-1 dims: `disjoint_span` and NdCopier skip them; their stride may be anything (RemoveDim
  push gives 0, remove_dim.rs:181-186; InsertDim pull gives 0, insert_dim.rs:178-183; user strides
  via plain_ndarray_ptr are kept verbatim in Plain pull results, plain.rs:465). `is_contiguous`
  demands exact default strides, so such outs take Scalar's strided path (conservative).
- Broadcast 0 strides: Scalar pull = all-zero strides, read-only (scalar.rs:98-102); Plain accepts
  0 strides and orders them outermost (plain.rs:142-159); a 0 stride on a len > 1 dim of an out is
  rejected by `disjoint_span` (itemsize > 0). Aliasing pull results are made read-only
  (broadcast.rs:160, ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs:949-953).
- Non-packed / permuted outs: honored via out strides; `alloc_out_buf` uses the storage's
  `read_layout_order`. Plain's order is built from a regular/broadcast/degenerate partition plus
  `read_layout_order_insert_dont_care_dim` (params.rs:921-928).
- NDIM_MAX: Index::new -> TooManyDimensions; `dim_arr` asserts (panic) elsewhere; Plain/Scalar
  constructors `check_ndim` (NEW: they take `&[u64]` now, plain.rs:117, scalar.rs:48).
- Unaligned: never required. Only Scalar's fast fill needs alignment and checks it
  (`is_contiguous_aligned`, buf.rs:243-247, then the cast_slice assert). dtype alignment of 64-bit
  types is hard-coded 8 on i686 (todo.md), >= ABI alignment.
- Struct dtypes / inner shape / itemsize != alignment: NdCopier copies by (itemsize, alignment)
  class (nd_copy.rs:30-38), padding copied as data; Scalar fast fill assigns T (padding of out
  left unspecified).
- bool8 / f16 / complex: no special handling here; bool8 accepts any byte by design.
- 32-bit: Plain `start as usize * stride` (plain.rs:457) truncates only when the address space
  could not hold the dim anyway (stride > 0) or the product is 0 (stride 0); `check_region_size`
  bounds Scalar `region_len` and `alloc_out_buf`. 64-bit: no isize::MAX bound on pull
  allocations (see Suspicions).
- Aliasing input vs out: only through unsafe constructors (from_raw_parts_mut over a Plain's
  memory; forbidden by buf.rs:94-97); span-level overlap of element-disjoint views is K111.

## Intentional behaviors

- No alignment required of a push out or promised of a pull buffer (core_trait.rs:88-92,
  buf.rs:22-24, plain.rs:89-89, 397; test plain.rs:797).
- Pull may lend a read-only view of the storage's memory or a 0-stride buffer
  (core_trait.rs:75-77). Read-only / aliasing pull results are rejected as `out` (test
  buf.rs:597-619).
- `check_out_buf` rejects a read-only out, a wrong stride count, a too-small out, and overlapping
  strides (tests buf.rs:564-595). The overlap check is conservative: interleaved layouts that do
  not overlap (lens (3, 2), strides (2, 3), itemsize 1) are rejected too (K103 note).
- Push writes only the region; bytes after it stay untouched (test scalar.rs:207-243).
- Empty regions are answered at the Array level: `to_buf_strided_into` with an empty region only
  checks stride count and writability (array/read.rs:433-434); `to_buf_slice` still demands the
  exact byte length (doc array/read.rs:252-252, error.rs:270-296).
- Bounds are re-checked at every level of a chain (todo.md "avoid calling check_get_range many
  times") - redundancy is known, not a bug.
- Plain/Scalar ignore `block_shape` / `block_shape_fixed_dims`; spec block shape is all 1s
  (plain.rs:82-83, 135-142; scalar.rs:52-59; test plain.rs:588). Params never change how a Plain
  buffer is stored (plain.rs:82-82). Scalar's `element_cost` is 0 and both set `plain_read`.
- Plain constructors reject negative strides on dims of length > 1 (InvalidArgument); any stride on
  a len <= 1 dim or in a zero-element array is replaced by the itemsize (plain.rs:512-524; test
  plain.rs:550-585). Python rejects negative strides too (jix-py/src/ops/common/operand.rs:508).
- `ArrayStorage` and `ElementType` are sealed (core_trait.rs:8-12, element_type.rs:16-16): user
  storages cannot exist; the unsafe code trusts crate impls (K50, K70 fixed).
- `Array::view()` returns `Array<&S>` (array/mod.rs:271); `&S` is transparent in `info()` (no
  "View" node, mod.rs:148-150). The `&dyn ArrayStorage` impl keeps the default
  `read_as_elementwise_pipeline` (pull + operand), so Scalar's `Constant` node is lost there.
- `write_out_buf_slot` forgets (leaks) a previously filled slot's buffer before its assert panics,
  to keep the drop off the panic path (buf.rs:509-513).
- `to_ndarray` layout is an implementation detail (array/read.rs:23).
- Open and acknowledged, do not re-report: K111 (Plain/numpy(out=) slices over the whole strided
  span alias element-disjoint views, todo.md); pull-mode `to_buf_strided` of O(1) lazy views copies
  the whole region (todo.md).

## Hot spots

- NEW Index chain: every `new_unchecked` caller listed in Contracts. Can any derived size be 0
  (zero-length concat member, tile/roll split piece, reshape split) or the start/size lengths
  differ (reshape changes ndim)? A 0 size reaching Plain underflows `(size - 1) * stride`
  (plain.rs:458: debug panic, release huge span into `from_raw_parts`); a length mismatch is UB via
  `assert_unchecked` (index.rs:93).
- NEW pull slot protocol: does every impl fill the slot exactly once on Ok, including early-return
  fast paths (slice.rs:148-171, broadcast.rs:156-162, read_data_and_map_strides)? Is a slot that
  an Err left filled ever reused (loops, retries, the cache path context.rs:210)?
- NEW push identity: can any push path assign `*out`, call `set_strides` / `make_readonly` /
  `with_offset` on the caller's out, or write via a buffer other than out? `materialize` hands
  back the caller's `&mut StridedBuf` (buf.rs:483).
- NEW `OutBuf::set` / `materialize` are SAFE but sound only after check_out_buf: any caller (op,
  FnStorage array/construct.rs:238, cache) that materializes before checking?
- NEW Shared buffers (buf.rs:63-66, 161, 337-348; #100 cache): `into_shared` turns a writable
  PoolBufMut pull result into a read-only Shared one - any consumer that expected to write into a
  pull result? Offsets carried through `with_offset` vs pool capacity; buffer returned to the pool
  (context.rs:199) while a Shared view still reads it?
- `check_out_buf_impl` (buf.rs:384-431): fast path (reverse dim order) vs sorted path agree?
  Stride ties, saturation, len-1 dims, PoolBuf capacity > logical size used as `len`.
- NEW `read_data_and_map_strides` (buf.rs:532-554, transmute gone): pull relabels a possibly
  writable buffer in place without `make_readonly` - do InsertDim/RemoveDim/PermuteDims maps keep
  it non-aliasing over the OUTER region?
- NEW forwarders (mod.rs:99-215): `&S`/`&mut S` replaced `View`; `Box` changes element type
  of the inner, Rc/Arc/&S wrap in IntoType. Any method left at its default that changes results
  or cache identity (`a.view() + a.view()`)? `ArrayStorageAny` caches shape/dtype/spec (any.rs:103).
- NEW Plain::read_data loop (plain.rs:448-460) and Scalar restructure (scalar.rs:92-121): two
  paths that must agree - Plain pull view vs push copy; Scalar contiguous fill vs strided copy;
  Scalar `read_data` vs `Constant` (scalar.rs:125-161, `N_OPERANDS = Some(0)`, ignores offset).
- `alloc_out_buf` (buf.rs:434-447): usize product unchecked on 64-bit; non-permutation layout
  order would give a writable aliasing buffer.
- Recent churn (git log 6dbeb15..HEAD on these files): #104 7ebac4c OutBuf; #103 c28c62a Index;
  #102 5ae28bf `&S` instead of View; #100 2d5e279 read cache (Shared variant); #98 fc0705b file
  moves (array.rs split into array/, elementwise_pipeline.rs moved to ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs);
  #95, #94 renames.

### Suspicions (unverified)

- [CONFIRMED in batch7-1 as K155] buf.rs:441-444 + error.rs:299 - on 64-bit nothing bounds a pull allocation by isize::MAX: e.g.
  `to_buf_strided` of the full region of a cheap lazy op over a scalar broadcast to
  [2^31, 2^32] u8 reaches `alloc_out_buf` and panics with capacity_overflow
  (util/aligned_vec/raw.rs:202-203) instead of the InvalidShapeOperation that 32-bit and
  `to_ndarray_sub` (array/read.rs:192-201) return. Low.
- [RULED OUT in batch7-1: same dtype goes to NdCopier; overlap needs unsafe constructors (K31/K111)] buf.rs:260-267 - `copy_from`'s Safety section omits NdCopier's no-overlap and dtype-class
  requirements (nd_copy.rs:46-55): a caller meeting the written contract can still be UB. Doc gap.
- [RULED OUT in batch7-1/7-2: derive(Dtyped) rejects padding (K110), Dtyped is unsafe] scalar.rs:99/120, scalar.rs:110-112, nd_copy.rs:30-38 - padded `#[derive(Dtyped)]` structs:
  uninit padding is viewed as `&[u8]` and copied as integers; the fast fill leaves out's padding
  unspecified, then compaction compresses those bytes (Miri-level uninit reads; low).

## Review units

- storage-core-buf-contract: jix/src/storage/core_trait.rs:1-200, buf.rs:1-555, index.rs:1-113,
  mod.rs:1-267, any.rs:1-110, info.rs:1-74 (~1340 lines). Consult util/nd_copy.rs,
  util/buf_pool.rs, util/mod.rs, context.rs, error.rs, array/read.rs,
  ops/shape_ops/{permute_dims,insert_dim,remove_dim,broadcast,slice}.rs, ops/into_type.rs,
  ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs. Focus:
  - NEW Index: can an empty or length-mismatched index reach a storage through any
    `new_unchecked` caller or the front doors (split_ranges after check_ranges)?
  - NEW OutBuf: slot filled exactly once on Ok; slot left filled on Err and reused; push paths that
    replace or relabel the caller's out.
  - NEW `OutBuf::set` / `materialize` / Shared + `into_shared`: safe fns with unchecked
    preconditions; writable-to-read-only conversion; pool return while a view is alive.
  - `check_out_buf_impl` disjointness and size check for every stride order and PoolBuf offset.
  - NEW `read_data_and_map_strides` without the transmute: lifetimes and aliasing of relabeled
    writable pull buffers.
  - NEW `&S`/`&mut S` forwarders and the `&dyn` impl: defaults that change behavior; Any metadata.
  - `alloc_out_buf` overflow (64-bit isize::MAX) and non-permutation layout orders.
- storage-core-leaf-backends: jix/src/storage/plain.rs:1-525, scalar.rs:1-182 (~730 lines).
  Consult storage/buf.rs, storage/index.rs, util/nd_copy.rs, util/mod.rs, storage/params.rs,
  element_type.rs, dtype.rs, error.rs, ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs, array/read.rs. Focus:
  - NEW Plain::read_data loop (no empty special case): offset/span math with len-1 dims carrying
    arbitrary user strides, 0 strides, 32-bit `start as usize`.
  - NEW `&[u64]` constructors with `check_ndim`: every shape validated before `DimDyn::from_slice`
    and `into_spec`? Plain's derived `read_layout_order` always a permutation?
  - `strides_from_ndarray` / `plain_ndarray_with`: offsets, empty arrays, negative strides on
    len <= 1 dims, owned vs borrowed.
  - Scalar push: contiguous fast fill vs strided copy (alignment assert, `region_len` vs the
    check_out_buf span, padding bytes).
  - Scalar `Constant` pipeline vs `read_data` (bool8, structs, zero-operand pipelines).
  - Plain `element_type_change` and unsafe constructor contracts vs what read_data does (K111 is
    open: do not re-report).
